name: showcase kit
summary: a reusable kit for turning codebases into portfolio case studies. repository probes, browser captures, structured project data, and a static-site builder bring the work together. the aaaflow showcase on this site was built with it.
problem: Turn a codebase into an understandable portfolio entry by combining repository facts, a written explanation, and captured media in a reusable format.
highlights: Repository probes: Collect deterministic facts such as languages, dependencies, routes, and Git information to support the project description.
Browser capture: Use a scripted Playwright tour to record a running application and produce screenshots and clips for the showcase.
Static publishing: Combine structured showcase entries into a self-contained portfolio with individual project views and responsive light/dark presentation.

media.caption: Actual showcase-kit build output for this portfolio, presented as a terminal capture.

sections.heading: The workflow
sections.body:
- Inspect the codebase and collect facts.
- Capture the running application's relevant workflows.
- Write a structured showcase entry and attach media.
- Build the static portfolio output.

sections.heading: Under the hood
sections.body: Python scripts handle probing, capture, and HTML generation. A JSON schema defines the content format, and the browser-capture step uses Playwright.

sections.heading: Scope & current state
sections.body: The kit was used for the existing aaaflow showcase on this site. Captures require a running app; static analysis alone cannot demonstrate runtime behavior.
